title: Tenant surge hedging and graceful eviction - PRD (wip)
content:
Context and motivation:

This doc sketches an approach for handling short-to-medium duration tenant demand spikes on Dedicated capacity while preserving predictable SLAs for paying tenants and keeping operational toil low. We want a middle path between: fully elastic (risky noisy neighbors / unpredictable latency) and strictly reserved (wastes headroom).

Goal (high level):
- Keep p99 latency SLOs for high-tier tenants during common surges (20-200% of baseline) without requiring immediate manual ops.
- Limit cost exposure from bursting while offering a deterministic fallback for overloaded tenants.
- Give tenants transparent controls and observable signals so they can opt into different risk/price tradeoffs.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity planning or committed billing contracts.
- We are not designing multi-cluster evacuation or operator-only emergency capacity in this doc.

Key concepts / vocabulary (working):
- Hedged Burst Credits: short-lived credit tokens allocated to tenants that can be consumed when load exceeds their baseline. Credits accrue and decay (aging) to discourage permanent over-commit.
- Graceful Eviction Lanes: ordered, policy-driven downgrade lanes (e.g., reduce max tokens/sec, drop lower-priority requests, redirect to hosted fallback) to shed load with observable degradation instead of hard failures.
- Isolation Envelopes: per-tenant runtime limits (queue depth, concurrent inflight, memory KV budget) that enforce bounded interference.
- Soft-Preemption: non-destructive interruption of lower-priority work (pause large batched jobs, stall background reranking) to free headroom quickly.
- Surge Hedging Window: short timescale window (30s–10m) during which system dynamically reshuffles spare capacity to cover spikes without immediate evictions.

Proposed high-level design:
1) Two-layer capacity model:
   - Reserved baseline: capacity tenant explicitly reserves/commits (billing/contract), guaranteed throughput within SLO.
   - Hedged pool + opportunistic pool: cluster-level pooled headroom (free for burst) and tenant-specific hedged credits.

2) Hedged Burst Credits mechanics:
   - Allocation: tenants receive a baseline daily credit budget proportional to historical peak or contract tier. Additional on-demand credits can be purchased or granted via opt-in policies.
   - Consumption: on traffic spike, tenant consumes credits to temporarily exceed their reserved baseline. Consumption is metered per-second and visible in console.
   - Replenishment and decay: credits replenish slowly (e.g., +X per hour) and decay over 48–72 hours if unused to avoid hoarding.
   - Throttles: once credits exhausted, tenant enters Graceful Eviction Lanes.

3) Graceful Eviction Lanes (GEL):
   - Lane 0 (transparent): slight request pacing (10-20% extra latency), continue serving normal priority requests.
   - Lane 1 (degradations): enable response compression, reduce max tokens/response, optional switch to distilled model variant.
   - Lane 2 (partial denial): drop background/low-priority routes, rate-limit per-key aggressive quotas.
   - Lane 3 (fallback): redirect to lower-cost hosted endpoint or return 429 with retry-after and guidance.
   - Transition rules: automatic transitions based on credit exhaustion + cluster congestion score + tenant tier. Backoff windows to avoid oscillation.

4) Isolation Envelopes and runtime enforcement:
   - Envelopes are a small set of runtime knobs: max_concurrent, queue_depth, kv_cache_budget, batch_size_cap.
   - Default envelopes per tier; advanced tenants can tune via console or API.
   - Enforcers exist in serving runtime and orchestrator to avoid cross-tenant GC/eviction cascades.

5) Smart routing & prewarm signals:
   - When tenant burns credits and demand persists, system triggers prewarm signals to spin up model warm instances in other node groups (with cost-aware routing).
   - Prewarm aggressiveness governed by expected surge persistence (short spikes: avoid full prewarm).

Operational behaviors and metrics to expose:
- Per-tenant credit balance (current, hourly delta), credit burn rate, time-to-empty forecast.
- Cluster hedged pool utilization, global opportunistic headroom, p50/p95/p99 latency per-lane.
- Eviction event logs (tenant, lane, reason, duration) and operator playbook links.

Pricing / billing considerations (sketch):
- Hedged credits included to varying degrees by tier (e.g., enterprise gets higher base replenishment).
- Overage model: burst consumption billed at a premium rate; optional monthly cap to limit cost surprises.
- Marketplace: option to buy one-off burst-pack credits via Console UI/API.

Example flow (simplified):
- Tenant T has baseline reserved 100 rps, historical peaks 250 rps. System assigns daily hedged credits that allow ~300s at +100 rps burst.
- Sudden spike to 500 rps. Tenant burns credits for first 120s. Cluster surge hedging window (180s) borrows opportunistic headroom and paces lower-tier workloads in GEL Lane 0.
- If spike persists beyond credit + hedging window, tenant moves into Lane 1 then Lane 2 depending on cluster score; console shows 'Entering Lane 1 - degraded responses' with ETA.

Operator playbook (ops-lite):
- Alert: cluster hedged pool < 15% + >3 tenants consuming >75% of their credits => pager to oncall.
- Quick actions: temporarily increase hedged pool by shifting low-priority tenants (only for emergencies), manually allocate emergency credits, or enable per-tenant grace windows.
- Postmortem: add trace of tenant burn + lane transitions to incident artifact.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (experiment): simulation + canary on single region; synthetic surges using workload-sim service.
- Phase 1 (beta): opt-in tenants only (enterprise beta): run live on small clusters, collect metrics and tenant feedback.
- Phase 2 (gradual): enable default conservative envelopes and small hedged credits for all Dedicated clusters.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- Credit economics: how to size replenishment rates so they’re useful but not exploitable? (need pricing model + simulation).
- Oscillation control: best hysteresis to avoid move in/out churn across lanes (cooldown timers, smoothing).
- Measurement cost: per-tenant fine-grained telemetry might be expensive at scale; what sampling/aggregation strategy?
- Legal / SLA language: how do we communicate lane-based degradation in contracts? Do we need new SLA tiers?

Implementation milestones (draft):
- Sim harness for credit & lane model (owner: eng/applied-ml) - 3 weeks
- Runtime enforcement for isolation envelopes (owner: serving-runtime) - 4 weeks + canary
- Orchestrator hedged pool allocator + console UI for credits (owner: platform-engineering + devex) - 3 weeks
- Ops runbook & alerting (owner: SRE) - 1 week

Back-of-envelope numbers to sanity-check (very rough):
- Typical hedged pool target: 5-12% of cluster capacity reserved as opportunistic headroom for short hedging windows.
- Credit replenishment: enough to cover 1–5 minutes of +X% sustained burst depending on tier.

Appendix / notes to self:
- Link to capacity-sim repo: github.com/redwood-inference/capacity-sim (experiment branch: surge-hedging).
- UX: console should show a small timeline view: credits remaining, lane history, last eviction.
- Quick comp: look at how streaming infra (video CDN) does token bucket + SLA lanes for inspiration.

Draft language for customer-facing one-pager (very rough):
"Redwood Dedicated now includes burst hedging and graceful degradation lanes to help applications survive short spikes without unexpected downtime. Customers can see burst credit consumption in real time and choose their preferred tradeoff between cost and availability."

Next actions (this week):
- Sync with Marcus/Oliver on sim requirements and initial parameters.
- Write a small experiment definition (load shapes: step, spike, ramp) and run against sim.
- Draft pricing options and share with finance for sanity check.

Unresolved: exact lane thresholds, precise billing multiplier for burst; need data from sim + beta to finalize.

----
Notes: keep this doc intentionally lightweight; this will likely merge into a longer PRD that covers related tenant fairness and burst-pricing mechanics. For now, focus on a simple, observable, and reversible set of behaviors to reduce manual ops during spikes.
content_summary: PRD draft for hedged burst credits, graceful eviction lanes, isolation envelopes, and operational plan for Dedicated capacity. Includes goals, high-level design, operator playbook, rollout phases, open questions, and next actions.
